assumptions: Synthetic feedback, not observed HK Express customer behavior.
Best tested feasible price pair, not a certified global optimum. Each round evaluates one candidate per track.
LLM and mathematical tracks have independent best prices; holdout only accepts or rejects each frozen candidate.
Contribution excludes mandatory pass-through fees and aircraft fixed costs.
Base NHPP parameters remain frozen. A run-local seat calibration layer learns only from completed training markets; holdout freezes the selected candidate profile.
Live work automatically crosses internal batches only within the explicitly authorized total decision limit; provider failures and the total cap stop execution.
One selected flight/date; V0 remains fixed while P is searched.
Profit is flight-attributed contribution: one third of new annual pass revenue and service cost, full per-flight costs; fees/taxes and aircraft fixed costs excluded.
Normal demand continuation is independently sampled from observed booking pace with random growth/jumps. The forecast does not generate its own evaluation labels.
Highest profit, highest margin and most buyers may be different tested prices; these are separate objectives.
Flights, personas, schedules, preferences, prices, arrival and cancellation paths are synthetic assumptions, not actual HK Express market shares.
The same seed creates identical latent background demand and customer occasions across policies. Demand never reads forecast means or quotas.

The NHPP receives completed as-of normal-booking intervals, excluding member seats. Fixed D28/D14/D7 rounds add max(0,total target minus all earlier valid unsold quota); FIFO consumption and cutoff expiry are explicit.

Unspent quotas persist until cutoff, but sales remain subject to physical capacity and normal-demand protection. Cancellation returns physical seats without minting quota. No new quota between rounds.
A pass discounts only its holder; companions pay normal fares. Every party purchase succeeds completely or not at all.
Pre-D28 bookings are existing occupancy; their sunk payments and operating costs are outside the comparative ledger.

Contribution includes per-trip costs, per-new-member service cost and one enabled-programme setup cost. It excludes mandatory pass-through fees and fixed aircraft costs; it is not total airline net profit.
Base fares and baggage are nonrefundable. All mandatory fees are refunded less the explicit cancellation service fee before cutoff; variable travel costs accrue at departure.

Membership must be valid at booking and departure, fee charged once in this run; every purchased term is observed to expiry. Every planned occasion is in the finite catalogue; the tail after the last occasion has explicitly no further planned trips, not censored usage. Renewal is an intention with an assumed next-period budget, never a paid conversion.
Only current reference offers are disclosed. WAIT never reserves inventory and no future prices, quotas, latent demand or counterfactual decisions are sent to agents.

Single selected-flight replay: one third of new annual pass income/service cost is attributed to this flight. Full fee is charged once; other trips are not simulated, so this is not annual profit or an optimal annual membership fee.

Buyers are distinct simulated customer households with an accepted booking, including later cancellations; tickets count their accepted party seats. Background requests are excluded. Fulfilled buyers/tickets count only flown bookings.
